scenarios.name: crawl-docs-into-rag-with-limits
scenarios.rationale: Response B uses Firecrawl crawl with an explicit limit (noting the 10,000-page default), includePaths, markdown scrapeOptions with onlyMainContent, and metadata.sourceURL as the chunk source, which covers the rubric. Response A never uses Firecrawl and builds a custom sitemap scraper, so it misses nearly every rubric item.

scenarios.name: extract-product-json-with-schema
scenarios.rationale: Both use a `json` format object with a schema and prompt, read `doc.json`, and state 1 base + 4 extra = 5 credits; B adds useful caveats (stealth proxy cost) and field descriptions, while A's Python/TS mostly equal but includes a caveat about guessing SDK details and uses a possibly less standard TS import.

scenarios.name: self-host-firecrawl-securely
scenarios.rationale: B covers nearly every rubric item: from-source Docker Compose with a checked-out release tag, port 3002, apiUrl/FIRECRAWL_API_URL, no-auth default, the AI provider needed for JSON extraction, and a pointer to SELF_HOST.md. A gives from-source compose and apiUrl but never checks out a release tag, omits the JSON-extraction AI provider warning (only mentions an optional OPENAI_API_KEY), and never points to SELF_HOST.md for exposure.
